note.explanation: In flowering plants, the diploid sporophyte makes haploid spores. These grow into small gametophytes, which make gametes. After fertilization, a diploid zygote develops into a new sporophyte.

The embryo sac is the female gametophyte.

written.text: Briefly describe the formation of egg cell and polar nuclei within embryo sac of a flower.
written.finalAnswer: The megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to produce four haploid megaspores. Only one remains alive. Inside it, mitosis forms eight haploid nuclei. Two nuclei move to the centre and fuse to form the fusion nucleus; one of the remaining six forms the egg cell.

written.text: Explain the lifecycle of flowering plants, focusing on the alternation between the gametophyte and sporophyte generations.
written.finalAnswer: The diploid sporophyte produces haploid spores by meiosis. In a flower, microspores develop into pollen grains, the male gametophytes, and a megaspore develops into the embryo sac, the female gametophyte. Gametophytes produce gametes. After pollination, the pollen tube carries two sperms into the embryo sac: one fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote, and the other fuses with the fusion nucleus to form a triploid nucleus that develops into endosperm. The zygote develops into an embryo; the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit. A seed can grow into the next sporophyte.

written.text: Describe how the female gametophyte (embryo sac) develops within the ovule of a flower.
written.finalAnswer: The ovule acts as a megasporangium and contains a diploid megaspore mother cell. It undergoes meiosis to produce four haploid megaspores, but only one remains alive. Mitosis forms eight haploid nuclei inside it. Two nuclei move to the centre and fuse to form a fusion nucleus; one of the remaining six forms the egg cell. The resulting female gametophyte, or embryo sac, has seven cells: one egg cell, one fusion nucleus, and five non-functional cells.

written.text: How do asexual and sexual reproduction contribute differently to genetic diversity of plant populations?
written.finalAnswer: Asexual reproduction usually produces offspring genetically identical to the parent, so it adds little genetic diversity. Sexual reproduction combines gametes and genetic material from two parents, producing variation among offspring and increasing genetic diversity.

written.text: How does the pollen tube facilitate the process of fertilization in flowering plants?
written.finalAnswer: When a pollen grain reaches the stigma, its tube cell forms a pollen tube. The tube grows through the stigma and style towards the ovary, enters the ovule through the micropyle, and carries the two sperms into the embryo sac so they can fuse with the egg and fusion nucleus.

examTips: Board questions commonly ask for definitions and roles of the sporophyte and gametophyte, or for the stages in the flowering-plant life cycle.
For the life cycle, give the sequence in order: meiosis and spores, gametophytes, pollination, pollen tube and two sperm fusions, then seed and fruit formation.
In questions on the embryo sac, include meiosis, four megaspores, the one surviving megaspore, mitosis, the fusion nucleus, the egg, and the seven-cell result.
For flower-part questions, match each whorl with its components and function where asked; use the terms anther, filament, ovary, style, and stigma precisely.
Marks are often awarded for distinct stages or named structures, so write each event as a separate clear point.

example.answer: The diploid sporophyte produces haploid spores; these develop into gametophytes that make gametes. Fertilization forms a zygote, which develops into the next sporophyte.

explain.title: Alternation of generations
explain.body: The major groups of plants have two type generations during sexual reproduction which come one after the other. These are sporophyte generation and gametophyte generation. The sporophyte generation produces spores which grow and make the new gametophyte generation. The gametophyte generation produces gametes which unite and make the new sporophyte generation. This phenomenon is called alternation of generations.

explain.title: Flower parts
explain.body: The four concentric whorls are calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), androecium (stamens), and gynoecium (carpels). A stamen has an anther and a filament. A carpel has an ovary, style, and stigma.

explain.title: Male and female gametophytes
explain.body: The microspore undergoes mitosis and forms a pollen grain, the male gametophyte. The ovule contains a megaspore mother cell; after meiosis and further development, one megaspore forms the female gametophyte, or embryo sac.

explain.title: Pollination and double fertilization
explain.body: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from an anther to a stigma. The pollen tube carries two sperms into the embryo sac. One fuses with the egg to form a zygote, and the other fuses with the fusion nucleus to form a triploid nucleus that develops into endosperm.

explain.title: Seed and fruit formation
explain.body: After fertilization, the zygote develops into an embryo and the triploid nucleus develops into endosperm tissue. The ovule matures into a seed and the ovary changes into a fruit.

mistakes: Do not confuse pollination with fertilization: pollination is pollen transfer from anther to stigma; fertilization is the fusion of gametes or nuclei.
Do not swap the male and female gametophytes: the pollen grain is male and the embryo sac is female.
Do not say both sperms fuse with the egg. One fuses with the egg and the other with the fusion nucleus.
Do not confuse the ovary and ovule after fertilization: the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.
Do not call the fusion nucleus triploid before sperm fusion; the sperm fuses with it to produce the triploid nucleus.
When describing embryo-sac development, include that only one of the four megaspores remains alive.
